findings.finding: The spec's 'How this is proven' names three checks, none of them a command with an expected output, and omits every CI gate the change's own non-Go files trip: claude-envoy's `bun run check-dist` for the committed bundle, envoy-go-race over ./internal/bus, the plain `go test ./...` of packages/envoy/infra that pins ListenerPermissions and the two gcp/testdata goldens, and the envoy-client and pi-envoy lanes.
findings.answer: Plan section 4 replaces the three checks with a twelve-row acceptance table, each row naming its surface and its exact command. Section 1 records, measured in this pod, which commands run here and which only CI can run, with the CI job named for each (AC7, AC8). The plan records this as spec departure 2.

findings.finding: 'Adopt PR #2101's work' does not say how its three commits cross a base main has moved past, and one of the three files main also touched, packages/claude-envoy/dist/envoy-channel.js, is a generated bundle whose hunk cannot be ported textually: CI's `bun run check-dist` rebuilds and compares byte for byte.
findings.answer: T1 starts fresh on legion/INFRA-113@origin (never a rebase, cherry-pick or jj duplicate of another App's commits). T2 adopts the eighteen untouched files verbatim with a named `jj restore --from fix/envoy-adhoc-topics@origin` and the full path list. T3 hand-applies the three drifted files onto main's current text and regenerates the bundle from tool-contract.ts under the pinned Bun. T4 keeps #2101's three-commit split and names each message.

findings.finding: The 400 refusal — the one behaviour change a human was asked about and chose — appears in no changelog entry and in none of the repository's endpoint contract tables. #2101's CHANGELOG hunk describes only the transport rule and the grant, and its new /v1/messages/publish row in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md says nothing about the refusal.
findings.answer: T5a makes it this issue's work: the CHANGELOG entry gains the status, the exact body and what the refusal closes, and the AGENTS.md row gains the same sentence. AC10 checks both at the head. The measured ground is in plan section 1: on the rig at current main, a publish to `$KV.envoy_roles.example-role` answered 200 and the bucket went from 0 to 1 message.

findings.finding: Four behaviour changes the spec names in passing have no check: the publisher receiving its own ad-hoc message, the non-agent exception lanes moving to the live path, the version-skew case, and a session with no NATS connection of its own receiving nothing. Two of them are promised to agents in text this change ships.
findings.answer: T5c adds the three exception-lane rows to the pure transport table test, which AC5 runs in the pod. Plan section 5 states the other three as claimed-not-checked, with the code that decides each: the listener's push fan-out always skips the source session (delivery.go:422, :638) and the durable never sees an ad-hoc topic, so self-receipt holds only for a self-subscribed session (pi-envoy's extensions/envoy.ts:1517) — which is exactly what #2101's text says, and the plan forbids simplifying it in review.

findings.finding: The caller census is asserted in the spec without saying what was searched, and its detail lives only on PR #2101, which this issue closes.
findings.answer: T5d requires the census to be re-run at the head and posted on the Dispatch issue as a comment when the new pull request opens, and names every caller found while planning, with file and line, plus the probe scripts to check before claiming none.

findings.finding: streamCaptures' literal-prefix assumption and the resulting transport of notifications.role.* and notifications.envoy.exceptions.* are nowhere stated.
findings.answer: Plan section 2 states the whole transport table as four rows and names TestEveryStreamSubjectIsALiteralPrefixAndWildcard as the guard it rests on. AC5 pins every row, exception lanes included.

findings.finding: The grant widening is asserted without showing the old enumerated list is a subset, or naming the other files that hold a copy.
findings.answer: Plan section 2 records it as settled: every entry of the old list begins with notifications., so the grant is a strict superset; HostPermissions inherits it (permissions.go:104-110) and SessionPermissions already subscribes notifications.> (permissions.go:88). AC6 runs the infra unit suite, which pins ListenerPermissions and both rendered cloud-config goldens with no Docker.

findings.finding: The spec does not say that the ListenerPermissions half landing on main changes nothing in production by itself, which is what a reviewer is most likely to assume it does.
findings.answer: Plan section 5 states it, AC12 makes it a criterion, and the PR body must carry it. The plan also fixes the expected production check: `pending`, because nothing deploys the hub, and the implementer does not invent a pass or ask a person to deploy.

findings.finding: Nothing says what happens to #2102 / INFRA-117 if review changes the code here, or whether the two diffs agreeing is part of this issue's acceptance.
findings.answer: Escalated. The architect answered part of it by Envoy message on 2026-10-22 and the plan records it in section 6: INFRA-117 is code-only (the twelve files of #2102), the ten documentation and client files stay on main with this pull request, and INFRA-120's session has agreed this pull request lands first. Who carries a review-driven change across remains the architect's open decision, named as such; the plan assumes nothing.

findings.finding: 'The Go tests of packages/envoy pass' has two readings that differ by a Docker-capable runner and by the integration suite, and no command from packages/envoy covers the infra module, which is a separate Go module outside the root go.work.
findings.answer: Plan section 1 and section 4 give the exact command list per module and per runner, and AC6 enters packages/envoy/infra on its own.

findings.finding: The 400 is inserted before the agent-topic refusal, changing the error one class of caller would get; neither the spec nor the PR body says the ordering was chosen.
findings.answer: Plan section 2 point 3 records that the orders are equivalent for every reachable input, because contracts.AgentTopicPrefix is itself `notifications.agent.`, and requires the PR body to say so, so the reviewer does not re-litigate it.

findings.finding: The spec rests on measurements outside this checkout (the hub VM, the deployment repository's pins and workflow, the branch's commit counts, the release versions) that a plan should not restate as its own evidence.
findings.answer: Plan section 5 cites them as the spec's evidence and forbids re-asserting them. Everything in plan section 1 was measured in this pod while planning.

findings.finding: 'Legion opens each pull request as its own and closes the earlier session's pointing at it' has no criterion at all.
findings.answer: AC11 makes it two commands with expected output: `gh pr view <n> --json headRefName,baseRefName,state,body` (head legion/INFRA-113, base main, body carrying `Dispatch: INFRA-113`) and `gh pr view 2101 --json state` (CLOSED). T7 names the close command and says #2102 is left open for INFRA-117.

specDepartures.spec: 'How this is proven' names three checks a machine runs on the change itself, the second of them 'The live permission tests of packages/envoy/infra pass against a real NATS server started with the permissions this change renders (go test -tags natslive ./core/, which needs Docker)', as a check this issue runs.
specDepartures.plan: The natslive check is claimed from CI's envoy-infra-go job by run id (AC7), because this issue's pod cannot run it. The implementer's and tester's own proof is a Docker-free rig committed at .legion/INFRA-113/rig/run.sh (AC1-AC4): the same authorization rendered by core.Authorization.Render from ListenerPermissions, a real nats-server at the hub's v2.15.1 with the hub's own arguments, the real cmd/listener binary, and a real credential-free core-NATS subscriber, with an origin/main listener as the negative control.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in this pod: no docker, podman, nerdctl or /var/run/docker.sock; packages/envoy/internal/testnats starts NATS through testcontainers (nats.go:107, :386), so `go test -tags natslive ./core/` dies at nats_auth_live_test.go:104 with `panic: rootless Docker not found`, as do ./internal/bus and ./cmd/listener. `go run github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@v2.15.1` does work, and the committed rig ran end to end in 15.8 s at current main: ad-hoc 500 after 5.002848 s with `Publish Violation`, captured topic 200 and received, $KV 200 with KV_envoy_roles going 0 to 1 message.

acceptance: AC7 is proven by CI's envoy-infra-go run id rather than by a command this issue runs.
AC1-AC4 add the Docker-free rig and its origin/main negative control as the implementer's and tester's own proof.

specDepartures.spec: The three checks of 'How this is proven' are the whole acceptance set the spec states, and 'Work that exists' describes #2101 as already holding the transport rule, the grant, the 400, the tests and 'the text that the fix made false'.
specDepartures.plan: The acceptance set is widened to twelve criteria, and four items are added to the work (T5): the 400 in the CHANGELOG entry and in the /v1/messages/publish row of packages/envoy/AGENTS.md; the now-wrong fanout-exception sentence at packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1841, settled with evidence rather than assumed; three exception-lane rows in the pure transport table test; and the caller census re-run at the head and recorded on the Dispatch issue.
specDepartures.evidence: #2101's CHANGELOG hunk (diff/6) describes only the transport rule and the grant, and its /v1/messages/publish row (diff/5) names no 400. packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1841 explains the explicit core publish of a fanout refusal by a reason the routing change removes, and #2101 does not touch it; publishDeliveryException forces PublishCore when fanoutRefusal (delivery.go:150-155) and the stream does capture the agent exception lane (stream.go:76), so dropping that branch would be a behaviour change, not a cleanup. Repository-wide, bus.ExceptionTopicPrefix + item.Topic is published only at delivery.go:140, and no pod-runnable test covers the transport of an exception on a non-agent, non-role topic.

outcome.scope: Four items added to the issue's work (T5a-T5d), each this issue's rather than a follow-up.
acceptance: AC5, AC6, AC9 and AC10 added: the pure transport table including the exception lanes, the infra unit suite and the goldens, the fresh claude-envoy bundle, and every text the change makes false being true at the head.
AC8 added: the remaining CI jobs this change's own files trip, cited by run id.
AC11 and AC12 added: the pull-request hand-over (#2101 closed pointing at the new one), and that nothing claims the hub is fixed.
